newsitem.title: USA: Stock prices off on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Stock prices off on profit taking.

text.p: Stocks fell Thursday as investors called time-out, one day after chasing the Dow Jones industrial average to its first close above 6,400 points.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow was off 19.75 points at 6,410.27, retreating from Wednesday's record close of 6,430.02, which was its tenth new high this month.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 12-9 on active volume of 270 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was off 6.45 points at 1,258.49, and the American Stock Exchange index lost 0.56 at 586.63.
Analysts said the selling was to be expected, especially given the tendency of investors to take profits at this time of the year for tax reasons.
"The market has become quite thin over the last week or so," said Christine Callies, chief investment strategist at CS First Boston.
She said the blue-chip market had raced up 18 percent since July, with few corrections along the way.

The losers included Intel, which was down 1-1/2 at 119-3/8, and Microsoft, off 1-1/2 at 151-3/4. International Business Machines, which led a late selloff in technology shares Wednesday, traded up 1/2 at 153-1/4.
"The well-known names have been overbought, and profit-taking in those names is taking the averages down," said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities.
She said that smaller stocks, which have not kept pace with the market, may get a boost soon.

"Some of the smaller cap stocks, particularly among the high techs, have not kept up with the household names," Farley said. "The cash coming into mutual funds and the cash being raised from tax-driven selling will be deployed in lesser-known names that are bargains."
Analysts said that the economic background continued to favour a market advance.
"So far it's just a little profit-taking, nothing lasting," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Corp. "The market is entitled to a little consolidation, even a correction.

"The background is favourable, indicating slow growth in the economy, no inflation pressures and no upward tendency in interest rates," he said. "That is the consensus and the figures have not shaken it."
Among special situations, Olsten Corp., the temporary-help firm, was down 5-5/8 at 14-1/4 after saying it expected fourth quarter earnings to come in below Wall Street estimates.

The selling spread to other companies also in the temporary-employment business. AccuStaff Inc. was down 3 at 20-1/2, Norrell Corp. lost 1-3/8 at 22-7/8 and Interim Services Inc. fell 2-3/8 to 36-3/4.
CompuServe Corp. fell 7/8 to 10-3/4 after the company said subscriptions to its main CompuServe Interactive online service declined slightly in the latest quarter.
